title: Claim is not idempotent over an existing same-assignee assignment
description:
`jit issue claim <id> <assignee>` hard-fails with "Issue is already assigned" even when the existing assignee is the claimant, so an assignment cannot be promoted into an in_progress claim.

## Background

Friction observed while lead-driving epic 2821e177 (2026-07-03, session 2). The assign-then-claim sequence is exactly what container stewardship produces: a lead assigns an issue while its dependencies are still open (a full claim would exit 4 on the blocked in_progress transition), and later — once dependencies complete — wants to promote that assignment into an in_progress claim. That promotion rejects, and the operator falls back to `jit issue update --state in_progress`.

This concerns claim being non-idempotent at promotion time over an existing same-assignee assignment, which is a separate lifecycle point from claim's behavior at intake time on a dependency-blocked container.

`jit issue claim` is assignment (it sets `assignee` and transitions state); it is distinct from the advisory `claims.jsonl` lease that `jit claim acquire` records and that requires a git worktree.

## Success Criteria

- [hard] REQ-01: `jit issue claim <id> <assignee>` on an issue already assigned to that same assignee proceeds rather than erroring — it retains the assignment and performs the Ready→InProgress transition once the issue is unblocked. Covered by a test: assign X while dependencies are open, complete the dependencies, then claim as X and assert the issue is InProgress with the assignee still X.
- [hard] REQ-02: `jit issue claim <id> <assignee>` on an issue already assigned to a different assignee continues to fail as today. Covered by a test asserting the rejection.

## Amendment A-8a15088a (invoker-approved, 2026-07-05)

REQ-01 originally read "records the lease ... assert in_progress with a live lease." `jit issue claim` does not record a `claims.jsonl` lease — that is the separate `jit claim acquire` command family (which requires git). The "lease" wording conflated the two subsystems. REQ-01 is reworded to describe what `jit issue claim` actually does: retain the assignment and promote to InProgress. Behavioral intent (idempotent same-assignee promotion) is unchanged.
